name: Dropbox
description: File storage and sharing service whose developer platform authorizes API access through OAuth 2.0 apps registered in its App Console.
notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Candidate families were enumerated from the Dropbox API documentation pages docs.dropboxapi.com (OAuth guide, Authorization, Authentication Types, Webhooks, Sharing; sources the OAuth page, -2835da9ecb, -ee9def1cd1, -66542bc3bd, -68ce992b0c) read raw on 2026-10-04; the list is what those pages name, not a complete inventory. Deliberately not candidates: the app key (client_id), an identifier carried in authorization URLs; the OAuth authorization code and PKCE code verifier, which are transient exchange values; the OIDC id_token; and shared links, which the Sharing page describes as publicly accessible links with optional expiry, password or team-only visibility, not as credentials issued to an app. Whether any of these deserves a family is left to a maintainer. Scanner rule artifacts were also read raw at pinned commits (Gitleaks config/gitleaks.toml, TruffleHog pkg/detectors/dropbox, Nosey Parker dropbox.yml, observed 2026-10-04) as artifacts, not as output on fixtures; only the access-token consistency claim reaches tool-corroborated. GitGuardian and GitHub secret-scanning pages were not read.
